corpus.why: Not under version control — none of its seven module directories is a git repository — so it cannot be pinned by commit. Frozen by copy and sealed by the layer-1 content digest, which is the assertion the git form also ultimately rests on. `.codegraph` is excluded so a stale index cannot make the no-graph arm accidentally find one; the build outputs are excluded because they are derived bytes that move without the source moving.

why: The second target, and the mandatory unavailability arm. Seven modules, JavaScript/Vue-dominant (480 .js, 123 .vue, 11 .ts) against wcp's Go/TSX — a different shape in module count, language mix and version-control status, all in mainstream languages. It is the only place `channel-unavailable{no-graph}` is exercised on real bytes, which is what keeps "the producer was unavailable" distinguishable from "the query matched nothing" — the distinction every later recall channel is measured against.

ablation.why: No ablation on this arm: with no graph there is no pool to ablate, and the assertions here are about the shape of unavailability rather than about vocabulary.
